title: Nebula Knowledge Stratification Ontology
description: Formal two-axis knowledge stratification ontology for Nebula. Controls how agents access the knowledge graph via abstraction level and visibility scope. Every document and chunk carries these two independent attributes.

abstraction_levels.description: Axis 1: Abstraction Level (L1–L4). Single-primary-level per chunk — no multi-level ambiguity. IMPORTANT: Level is an abstraction/explanatory altitude, NOT a rank. It does not rank truth, confidence, importance, visibility, lifecycle, or authority. Authority lives with the owning systems and admission paths; visibility is a separate scope. A higher level is a different altitude of explanation, not 'better' or more senior. The same canonical subject may carry L1, L2, L3, and L4 projections simultaneously; level belongs on the projected assertion/version, never the canonical asset identity.

L1.name: Evidence / mechanics
L1.description: What happened and how it works at the operational level — build details, APIs, schemas, method contracts, error codes, config values, execution evidence

L2.name: Semantic structure
L2.description: How data and state are organized — subsystem design, DAG semantics, traversal behavior, data models

L3.name: Architecture / rationale
L3.description: Why the system exists and the reasoning behind its shape — migration philosophy, architectural rationale, trade-offs, subsystem relationships

L4.name: Doctrine / governing interpretation
L4.description: The rules and boundaries that govern the system's own operation — cross-system doctrine, ontology definitions, role boundaries, ownership and governance rules

rules: SINGLE_PRIMARY_LEVEL: A chunk targets exactly one abstraction level — no multi-level ambiguity
CHUNK_CAN_OVERRIDE_DOCUMENT: Chunks can override their parent document's dominant level when content diverges
CONTENT_NODE_OWNS_LEVEL: Content nodes own the abstraction level — cross-reference edges remain level-neutral
LEVEL_NOT_A_RANK: Level is abstraction/explanatory altitude, never a ranking of truth, confidence, importance, visibility, lifecycle, or authority

LEVEL_ON_PROJECTION: Level belongs on the projected assertion/version (or versioned projection), never the canonical asset identity — a level change produces a new projection/version, never a silent mutation
LEVEL_ORTHOGONAL_TO_VISIBILITY: A chunk's abstraction level (L1–L4) is independent of who may see it (visibility scope)
DEFAULTS_NOT_SOURCE_LABELS: Level defaults are content-determined, not source-system labels — e.g. a model-check result is L1 execution evidence even if produced by Aegis; its interpretation is L3
UNKNOWN_LEVEL_STAYS_EXPLICIT: Unknown or disputed levels remain explicit rather than being guessed; a disputed level is recorded as such

chunk_kinds.description: The 12 ChunkKind enum values classify the type of content within a chunk.

visibility_scopes.description: Axis 2: Visibility Scope. Controls which roles can see a given chunk.

role_query_filters.description: Per-role query filters that control access projections over the single shared knowledge graph. IMPORTANT: These describe the altitude each role typically starts from for retrieval and explanation — NOT permissions, clearances, or a rank ordering. The level_filter predicates are retrieval preferences (which altitude a role's query defaults to), not a promotion above another role; any role may move between altitudes explicitly, and a 'broader' starting range is a wider angle of explanation, not a seniority boost.

builder.cross_reference_detail: Only when blocked or asked for context — e.g., 'why does this API exist?' expands to L2 rationale

architect.cross_reference_detail: Expanded for design context — traces design lineage via cross-references

reviewer.cross_reference_detail: Cross-ref to verify implementation matches spec

inspector.level_filter: level ≤ 3 with preference for normative chunks
inspector.cross_reference_detail: Aggressive cross-ref expansion for compliance auditing — lineage tracing

cross_reference_semantics.description: Cross-references are a conditional expansion operator, not a default join. They create edges between artifacts that are traversed only when the agent's context demands it.
cross_reference_semantics.guiding_principle: We distribute access projections over a single knowledge graph, not distribute the knowledge itself. Every agent sees a filtered view of the same graph, tuned to their role's abstraction level and visibility scope. Cross-references are the mechanism for expanding that view when context demands it.

integration.description: This ontology layer sits above the existing DDL infrastructure. It provides the semantic classification rules that the DDL implements as columns and constraints.
